courseTitle: Ionic - Build iOS, Android & Web Apps with Ionic & Angular

cues.en: Now we had a look at global theming,
what if you don't want to use the same theme
or maybe just on one component, not the same styles on both platforms?
The good thing about Ionic is it by default adjusts the styles based on the platform it's running
on. The tabs behave differently, for example there is a ripple effect when we're running on the iPhone
than when we're running on the Pixel here, you always need to reload after switching the device
by the way, here we got that ripple effect,
we got a different spinner, we got different tabs with a ripple effect and for example the hamburger
icon here also is not colored because that doesn't fit the Material Design Guide.
So we got these platform adaptive styles out of the box which is a big selling point of Ionic because
it makes it easy for us to build cross-platform applications with one codebase that still look and
feel native-like but sometimes you just want to overwrite something or you want to have your
own main color set or a different primary color for a different platform.
Well then, you can take advantage of something you can see when you go into the elements tab in your
developer tools. On the root.html element, you will see that there are a couple of classes applied
and there also is a mode. Now that is all set automatically by Ionic based on the mode or the platform
it detects.
Now it does detect this simply by the headers sent for example,
so if you're previewing this here in an Android phone, indeed the mode is set to md for material design
and you also have the md class here
and if you're switching to an iPhone and you're reloading, then this actually is set to iOS as you can
tell.
Now if you're viewing this on a desktop, so without being in this preview of a mobile device, then you
see it's actually using Material Design as a default.
Now this is nice but how does this help us?
Well since we got a class here, md or iOS, we can of course take that into account when setting up our
styles and that does not only include styles anywhere in our components or our custom CSS rules
but I'm also talking about this general setup.
This root selectorr here is a pseudo selector that simply selects the root element in your application,
typically the HTML element and then the variables here therefore apply to the entire application
but you can also of course add a class selector for iOS if you want to set up iOS specific styles
or markdown.
Now what I mentioned earlier is that you of course could say for iOS ion-button,
so for all buttons that are running in the iOS mode or for all divs that are running in the iOS mode or
for all items with my own class, my own class in iOS mode, you can set up your own rules
but of course you can also just select iOS and then just as we do it here, set up some general styles.
So for example here just to demonstrate this, if I set up my primary color to be totally different, let's
say green, just as a demo not because it's so beautiful for iOS, then you will see that as this reloads,
on the desktop
we still have the red color,
if I go into the mobile view though and I'm on an iPhone here and I reload, I have that green primary color.
So this allows you to adjust styles on any level, be that the global level here or on a component or
a custom CSS rule level based on the platform with the help of the iOS class and the material design
class selectors added automatically or the classes are added automatically by Ionic.
